title: Classify positive rational diagonal metrics with universal full anchor boxes
body:
PR5172 leaves open which positive rational metrics diag(1,d,1) retain a full directed anchor box for every rational three-column factor with nonempty canonical ties. This package proves the exact criterion: v2(d) is even and the normalized odd unit is1 modulo4. It includes nonsquare positive cases such as d5, and explicit counterexample families for every complementary class.

The proof preserves the original whole-instance anchors exactly under dual power-of-two column scaling, then uses the credited modulo-four F/O/L labeling construction. It includes inactive columns and negative valuations; no row subset is renormalized. The new odd-valuation family already gives d2 with M=diag(2,4,4), anchors A=(5,7,7), B=(5,5,5), and exact box2. The even-valuation negative family generalizes the retained d3 four-row obstruction.

Validation: independent scoped proof review found no blocker; registered normal/optimized exact checks pass100 positive and36 negative family fixtures, the authenticated definition-level d2/d3 oracle and10 semantic/type controls. Metadata, committed-byte/source-history checks and official12-file export pass. Git-free normal/optimized replay passes; missing RESULT/SOURCES, changed source bytes and equal-valued numeric type receipt mutations reject. Finite checks corroborate the written universal proof rather than establish it.

Credit Nick Petalas PR5172 for the fixed positive-metric obstruction and classification question, Sagar Thakrar PR3612 for the rational Gram theorem and original-anchor coloring, and Aaron Wang/navinor and DreamingOfClouds's retained anchor/F-star lineage. Prepared by JoyboyBrian with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

Scoped algebraic classification only: no arbitrary asymmetric F-star theorem, physical supplier, COPY/routing/precision/tape improvement, new kappa or selected-frontier change. Human and formal proof-kernel acceptance remain unclaimed. The next question is arbitrary positive diagonal triples, requiring a separate proof rather than automatic expansion.
